manifest.name: LeKiwi (stock)

kinematics.scale_note: URDF lengths are metres, the referenced meshes are millimetres and carry no <mesh scale>; multiply link poses by 1000 after FK (or the meshes by 0.001 before).
kinematics.joint_limits_source: Source: TheRobotStudio/SO-ARM100, Simulation/SO101/so101_new_calib.urdf (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheRobotStudio/SO-ARM100/main/Simulation/SO101/so101_new_calib.urdf, fetched 2026-09-12) -- the only SO-101 description that carries <limit> tags. Its <limit> values, in degrees: shoulder_pan +-110, shoulder_lift +-100, elbow_flex +-96.83, wrist_flex +-95, wrist_roll -157.21..+162.79, gripper -10..+100. The LeKiwi URDF (external/LeKiwi/URDF/LeKiwi.urdf) has NO <limit> tags and, more importantly, a DIFFERENT joint zero: its zero pose is the folded/parked CAD configuration (upper arm horizontal backwards, forearm folded forward again) while the reference zero has the upper arm up and the forearm forward. The mapping q_lekiwi = sign * q_ref + offset_deg was solved geometrically, not guessed: both URDFs describe the same physical arm, so for each joint the axis LINE (point + direction) of every downstream joint must coincide once the two chains are aligned by one rigid transform. Fitting sign+offset per joint over 6-8 random configurations leaves max axis-line offset 5.1 mm and max axis-angle 0.87 deg (identity mapping: 254 mm / 180 deg; the best wrong sign combination: 145x worse cost), the residual being the genuine CAD difference between the two exports (forearm 136.0 vs 135.0 mm, two DH offsets 1.5 and 3.5 mm apart). Signs: pan +1, lift/elbow/wrist_flex/wrist_roll/gripper -1 -- i.e. every LeKiwi arm axis except the shoulder pan points the opposite way to the SO-101 reference axis. The pan offset is not observable from geometry (a base rotation absorbs it) and is taken as 0, which is correct by inspection: at pan 0 the arm points robot +Y in both models, and the limit is symmetric anyway. The gripper offset is likewise not observable from the axis lines (nothing is downstream of it), and a mesh test cannot find it either: the stock jaw pivots INSIDE its own bracket, so Moving_Jaw_08d-v1 intersects Wrist_Roll_08c-v1 at every angle from -120 to +103 deg in the decimated meshes. It is taken as 0 on the finger-tip measurement instead: tip separation (moving-jaw tip to fixed-finger tip, collide.js gripOpening) falls monotonically 142.2 mm at -100, 62.7 at -30, 41.6 at -15, 20.1 at 0, 7.1 at +10, with its minimum 6.2 mm at +15 -- so LeKiwi arm_gripper 0 is the near-closed jaw exactly as the reference's 0 is, +10 is the closed stop (matching the reference's 10 deg of over-close) and NEGATIVE arm_gripper OPENS. This also agrees with the app's own presets, which use arm_gripper -30 for the two reaching poses. SANITY: the LeKiwi URDF zero pose (all six joints 0) lands inside every one of these ranges, 3.8..69.3 deg from the nearest stop -- as a parked CAD pose should. CAVEAT for the app: three of the four presets shipped in v3 were authored before any limit existed and fall OUTSIDE this range -- stowed (lift +40, wrist_flex -54), reach floor (lift +20, elbow -76), reach table (lift +9). Only 'raised max' is legal. Independently of the limits, collide.js finds those same three presets to be in HARD COLLISION with the robot (upper arm through Base_08q / the WaveShare plate / the deck plate), so they are not merely out of travel, they are impossible. See the SO-101 motion reference for IK-corrected replacements that hit the same tip positions. arm_joint_range_deg above is the OLD UI travel hint and is kept only so that nothing that reads it breaks; joint_limits_deg is the physical one.
kinematics.zero_pose_note: The URDF zero pose is the folded/parked CAD configuration, NOT the SO-101 reference zero; joint_limits_map carries the sign+offset that relates the two. All six joints at 0 is inside every limit.

deck_grid.note: top deck plate bolt grid: 20 mm pitch, Z 57, usable radius 107, hole Ø3.50 (M3 clearance), measured on the deck mesh

wrist_flange.axes: +X = the arm_wrist_roll axis (finger direction), +Z = -arm_gripper hinge axis, +Y = Z x X
wrist_flange.note: PincOpen assembly frame -> robot frame at the arm ZERO pose. APPROXIMATE, derived from the stock gripper. +X = the arm_wrist_roll axis (0,0.42262,-0.90631), the stock finger direction. +Z = -arm_gripper hinge axis (0,0.90631,0.42262), so the PincOpen camera stack points the same way as the stock wrist camera bracket. +Y = Z x X = robot -X, the stock jaw opening direction. Origin: the PincOpen back face (full-gripper X_min = -53.49 mm) is put on the wrist-roll output flange; the stock fixed jaw starts 1.0 mm behind it. The PincOpen mirror plane Y=0 and finger mid-plane Z=0 are put on the stock gripper centreline. Assumed: PincOpen bolts straight onto the wrist-roll flange with no adapter plate; no CAD of the real adapter was available. Expect a few mm of error along +X.

cameras.label: Front
cameras.name: Front (navigation)
cameras.note: DEVICE ONLY - this entry is the camera, not a mount. The fitted front camera option publishes the pose: the stock bracket carries the URDF datum, and removing it switches the camera off.
cameras.pose_derivation: camera <- Camera-Model-v3 link frame (mm), column-major: col0 = image right, col1 = image up, col2 = -optical axis, col3 = sensor point. Derived from the URDF visual origin of the link (xyz -0.01601 0.00243 -0.01139, rpy 1.74533 1.39626 -pi) plus meshes/Camera-Model-v3.stl: a 38 × 38 × 3 mm board at mesh z 0..3 with an M12 lens barrel (r 6.1..6.8) from z 3 to 21.5, so the optical axis is mesh +Z and the sensor is the board front face, mesh (0,0,3). At the base pose that is robot (0, 111.75, 25.05) aiming (0, 0.98481, 0.17365) = +Y, 10.000° ABOVE horizontal (verified: the axis ray clears Camera-Mount-v8 and every stock mesh, never meets the ground, and matches a photograph of the real front feed). robot_matrix is the same pose already multiplied through FK, used when ctx.fk cannot resolve the link.

source.derivation: All three cameras on the robot are the JR DF200 "100° without distortion" module, streamed MJPG at 640 × 480 (user-confirmed 2026-09-15). 100° on the DIAGONAL of a rectilinear 4:3 frame is 2*atan(tan(50)*4/5) = 87.3° horizontal, 2*atan(tan(50)*3/5) = 71.1° vertical. This is a hardware fact, not a fit: the fitted numbers this package shipped before are the alternatives beside it.

alternatives.label: measured from the top feed
alternatives.note: A two-landmark (front omni-wheel tops) fit of one screenshot of the live top feed. It is under-determined - tilt and FOV trade against each other - and at the confirmed 87.3 the same screenshot no longer reproduces: its wheel spacing and its silhouette scale want 60-66. The screenshot is most likely a crop. Kept so the old coverage numbers can be reproduced.
alternatives.url: measured: fit of the live top-camera feed, 2026-09-12

alternatives.label: measured from the wrist feed
alternatives.note: A three-landmark (servo LED, gripper body top edge, fingertip) least-squares fit of the real wrist feed: 32.7° half-vFOV, i.e. 65.4° V = 81° H at 4:3. The three landmarks solved separately give 74.6 / 83.3 / 90.8, mean 82.9 - the confirmed 87.3 is inside that spread.
alternatives.url: measured: least-squares fit of the real wrist image, 2026-09-13

alternatives.note: The camera the upstream LeKiwi BOM lists for base_camera_mount.stl: Arducam 5MP OV5648 wide-angle USB, "Field of View (FOV): 90 degree (H)", M12 lens. It is the camera the URDF models; it is not the one on this robot.

alternatives.note: Arducam B0454, "5MP OV5648, 110 Degree DFOV Wide Angle". 110° on the diagonal of a rectilinear 4:3 frame is 97.6° H / 81.2° V.

alternatives.note: The 2026-08 coverage sweep assumed a 90° diagonal lens as ±33° horizontal and ±25° vertical, i.e. 66° H. That is conservative: a rectilinear 90° diagonal at 4:3 is 77.3° H. Kept so the old coverage numbers can be reproduced.

manifest.presets_source: Four arm poses, corrected against the joint limits. The set this studio shipped earlier was authored before any limit existed: three of those four broke a limit and were in hard collision with the robot, so these replacements hit the same tip positions from inside the limits. One example: Reach floor holds arm_wrist_flex at 170.5, not the 171 the earlier table printed, because 171 is 0.5° past the -19.5..170.5 stop. Angles are degrees in the LeKiwi URDF convention; kinematics.joint_limits_map relates them to the SO-101 reference zero.

mass.source: Upstream publishes no weight. Seeed Studio LeKiwi Kit 12 V (base, printed parts, battery, no Pi, no cameras, no arm) is listed at 1.7 kg. Add the Raspberry Pi 5 with its cooler (0.06 kg), two USB cameras (0.02 kg), the six arm STS3215 servos at 55 g each (Feetech, 0.33 kg) and the printed SO-101 arm parts by the sim's volume rule (0.34 kg). The band is that 2.45 kg ±15 %.

manifest.name: PincOpen
manifest.description: Pollen Robotics PincOpen - a printable parallel gripper for the SO-101 wrist, with a camera seat on the top plate.

source.files: meshes/ = cad/stl, all 14 originals, copied verbatim - see SOURCE.md

frame.notes: PincOpen assembly frame, mm: Y = 0 is the jaw mirror plane, +X is the fingertip direction (nose at X = 70.64), Z is the finger width axis (±12.86). Mounts on a host robot at its wrist flange; the host supplies the placement.
frame.mount_note: the back face of the assembly (X min) seats on the wrist-roll output flange

derivation.what: PincOpen ships 14 loose STLs and no assembly information, so each original was registered against the connected bodies of the in-place assemblies below. Those assemblies are built from these same files by mesh CSG in the assembly frame. Parts are matched by sorted bounding-box extents, not by volume: several upstream STLs report a wrong mesh volume. The pose is then solved by ICP - iterative closest point, the standard rigid fit of one point set onto another - seeded from all 48 signed principal-axis permutations, and a rigid fit is preferred over a reflected one. The residual is the point-to-surface distance of 4000 surface samples.
derivation.residual_note: A residual is the distance from the ORIGINAL mesh, placed by the solved transform, to the surface of the assembled body. Zero means the body is that part, exactly, there. The non-zero ones are local surface differences introduced by the CSG rebuild that produced the in-place assembly, not pose error: every one of them has a bounding box that matches the original to 0.000 mm.
derivation.not_placed_note: These parts do not appear in either in-place assembly, so no placement could be derived; they are listed under `spares` with their own CAD frame.

interference_audit.mesh: measured on meshes/STS3215_03a-v1.stl at 6506 faces, watertight - NOT on the decimated copy in src/data/assets.js (FACE_CAPS caps STS3215* at 6000), which will read slightly differently
interference_audit.top_plate: a 0.028 mm skin where the motor's nose face (X -7.800) meets the Top_Plate's inner wall (X -7.83). Same order as the 0.025 mm tab-hole residual: registration noise, and it CONFIRMS the X placement rather than contradicting it.
interference_audit.motor_flange: 86 of the 90 mm³ sit at Z 39.1..40.8, i.e. ABOVE the motor's own back face: the mesh's PASSIVE REAR HORN, a d20 × 1.8 mm disc PincOpen does not fit (its flange straps straight onto the back). Cut the mesh at the back face and 90 -> 3.7 mm³, which is the 0.04 mm skin on one fork leg - the registered flange is 12.46 / 12.36 about Y = 0 against the motor's ±12.40.
interference_audit.camera_basement: the same rear horn. 83 -> 0.02 mm³ below the back face. The basement is also the UPSTREAM camera mount, an alternative to whatever sits on the seat.
interference_audit.cam: the drawn splined shaft (d5.4, on X -18) inside the Cam's central bore, 1.25 mm deep - the DRIVE COUPLING. PincOpen puts a Feetech spreader-bar horn on that shaft and screws the Cam to the bar with 5 screws (assembly guide steps 18 and 32); the URDF draws an integrated disc horn with the shaft 1.5 mm proud of it instead.
interference_audit.is_it_a_placement_error: No. Sweeping Z by ±0.60 mm trades the two: flange 58 -> 121 mm³ while cam 116 -> 7 mm³, and neither reaches zero. The overlaps are 1.0-1.6 mm DEEP - 40 to 60 times the 0.025 mm tab-hole residual - so they are geometry, not placement. Z stays where the motor's shoulder seats on the Top_Plate slot rails (residual 0.0000 mm), which is PincOpen's own assembly datum (step 31).

placement.interference_note: Every number above the back face (Z 39.0025) is the mesh's PASSIVE REAR HORN (d20 × 1.8 mm) and its 6-pin plug stub, which PincOpen does not fit; cut the mesh at the back face and the flange falls to 3.7 mm³ and the basement to 0.02. The 16.7 mm³ at the Cam is the drawn splined shaft inside the Cam's central bore - the drive coupling, not a clash. For scale, the URDF's own servo/bracket pairs interpenetrate 375-399 mm³ at the wrist.

manifest.cameras_note: The upstream Cam.stl is placed by this package, but PincOpen publishes no sensor or lens for it, so no hFOV is claimed here. The camera a host robot actually mounts on frames.camera_plate is declared by that host - see the lekiwi-pincopen package, cameras.wrist.

kinematics.links_note: body = the fixed plates and everything bolted to them; rod_* / rod2_* = the two bars of each four-bar (Internal_Rod and External_Rod); finger_* = the couplers (-Y = L, +Y = R) that carry Distal_Rod, Distal_Shell, Tip_Support and Removable_Tip; jaw_ref carries no geometry and exists only as the control joint's child.

joints.name: jaw
joints.zero: fully closed - the exported state of every STL in this package
joints.note: DEGREES, and an OPENING ANGLE, not a distance: q = 30.0007° - theta, where theta is the crank angle of either bar measured from +X. 0 = fully closed (the exported state of every STL here), 30.0007 = wide open (a 40.0 mm gap). `jaw_ref` carries no geometry; the six joints below mimic this one and carry the two bars and the coupler of each side. The finger does NOT slide: it travels on the four-bar arc, so it also moves +5.359 mm along +X between closed and wide open. See kinematics.control_display.jaw for the millimetre gap a slider should show.

joints.name: jaw_rod_L
joints.note: the -Y Internal_Rod: the first bar, turning about the ground pivot (0.00, -32.50). It mimics `jaw` with multiplier -1, which is the only place the mirror sign is written down.

joints.name: jaw_rod2_L

kinematics.hinges_note: all hinge axes are parallel to Z; quoted for the -Y finger and mirrored in Y for the +Y one. Upstream uses M3 self-tapping screws, d3.00 anchor holes and d3.25 running holes (pincopen_mods/README.md)

linkage.coupler_motion: pure translation on an arc (the finger does not rotate, but it does move in X as well as Y)
linkage.finger_travel_note: the -Y finger's displacement from closed to wide open, [dX, dY]. dX is the part a prismatic model throws away.
linkage.bars_note: Reference data for the two bars of the -Y side (mirror Y for +Y). The bars are REAL LINKS on real revolute joints now, so nothing has to animate them: FK moves them, the collision world poses them, and their distal pivots stay on the finger pivots at every jaw angle.
linkage.derived_from: the four hinge coordinates in the PincOpen mods README (off-repo), reverse-engineered there from the meshes and verified by point containment

jaw.label: opening gap
jaw.note: The control joint is an ANGLE; what a user wants to dial is the gap between the fingers in millimetres. A UI that understands `kind` may show the slider in `unit` over `range` and convert on the way in and out; one that does not still gets a correct degree slider.

stroke_mm.source: derived from the linkage geometry, NOT an upstream specification - upstream publishes no joint range
stroke_mm.closed_gap_note: measured between the two registered Tip_Support meshes along Y. The exported state is fully closed, so this is the manufacturing clearance at the contact face, not a design gap.

verified.how: the two Tip_Support meshes were posed through the chain at each jaw angle and measured along Y; the bar check transports each bar's distal pivot through FK(bar link) and the same point through FK(finger link) and compares them.

fingertips.label: Fingertips
fingertips.hint: The tip support that bolts to each finger on the 3x M2 pattern (X 51.64 ±3.5 and X 61.64, blind from the Y = -7.75 face).

interface.holes_axes: X, Z in the assembly frame; blind into the finger from the Y = -7.75 face
interface.screw: M2 self-tapping (d2.05 pilot), or M2 heat-set inserts with the E mod (d3.00)

fingertip_pad.note: centre of the 3x M2 tip pattern on the -Y finger; mirror in Y for the +Y finger

camera_plate.holes_axes: X, Y in the assembly frame, at Z = 19.50 (the Top_Plate camera face)

manifest.name: LeKiwi + PincOpen
manifest.description: LeKiwi with the PincOpen gripper on the wrist, the over-the-shoulder corner mast carrying the top camera, the DF200 forward arch carrying the wrist camera and the vertical Pi case. Every slot offers the design that is on the robot, the stock LeKiwi or PincOpen part where there is one, nothing at all, and an import.

source.note: geometry inherited from the lekiwi package; the gripper comes from the pincopen package (CC-BY-SA-4.0); the parts are this project's own

attach.note: The PincOpen assembly frame IS lekiwi.frames.wrist_flange, by construction: that frame was derived so +X is the finger direction and the gripper's back face lands on the wrist-roll flange, so the attachment local is the identity. PincOpen assembly frame -> robot frame at the arm ZERO pose. APPROXIMATE, derived from the stock gripper. +X = the arm_wrist_roll axis (0,0.42262,-0.90631), the stock finger direction. +Z = -arm_gripper hinge axis (0,0.90631,0.42262), so the PincOpen camera stack points the same way as the stock wrist camera bracket. +Y = Z x X = robot -X, the stock jaw opening direction. Origin: the PincOpen back face (full-gripper X_min = -53.49 mm) is put on the wrist-roll output flange; the stock fixed jaw starts 1.0 mm behind it. The PincOpen mirror plane Y=0 and finger mid-plane Z=0 are put on the stock gripper centreline. Assumed: PincOpen bolts straight onto the wrist-roll flange with no adapter plate; no CAD of the real adapter was available. Expect a few mm of error along +X.

manifest.hide_note: the WHOLE stock gripper - fixed jaw (Wrist_Roll_08c-v1), moving jaw and jaw servo - comes off and PincOpen bolts to the wrist-roll horn; the stock wrist camera is replaced by the DF200 arch; the stock flat Pi case is replaced by the vertical rev-I case (it also fouls the mast legs). These are MESHES: the links of the same names, and the frames on them, stay.

deck_rear_pocket.note: XY centre of the rev-I Pi case footprint (X ±43.75, Y -91.8..-51.5)

verified.against: the DF200 wrist arch as shipped: assets/parts/df200_arch/part.json -> cameras.wrist, folded through frames.wrist_flange. The PincOpen assembly frame IS that frame, so the fold is the identity.
verified.droop_note: unmeasured - nothing has been photographed through this bracket yet.
verified.framing_source: gen_wristcam_arch.framing_table() and its landmark table, at hFOV 87.3° (half-vFOV 35.582°)
verified.gates: Gates: the servo LED and the servo nose out of frame by at least 4.7° at every pupil offset in the bracket, |v_grasp| <= 1, and both pads in frame closed and at 40 mm open. At hFOV 87.3° only 30° and 35° pass, by 9.25 and 1.96° of LED margin over the gate. The rest fail the LED gate: 40° by 5.31°, 45° by 12.56°, 50° by 19.79°, 55° by 26.99°, 60° by 34.16°. 35° is shipped as the steeper of the two that pass, so it keeps the most gripper-relative resolution.

cameras.note: DEVICE ONLY - the mount pose is published by the fitted `wrist_camera_mount` option, in the `wrist_flange` frame, so it follows the arm. The default (df200_arch) puts the sensor at (-19.96, 0.00, 99.23) in the PincOpen assembly frame, 35° below the finger direction (+X); the stock SO-101 bracket is on `stock`, and `pincopen_holder` / `none` publish `null` - the camera is off.

source.derivation: All three cameras on the robot are the JR DF200 "100° without distortion" module, streamed MJPG at 640 × 480 (user-confirmed 2026-09-15). 100° on the DIAGONAL of a rectilinear 4:3 frame is 2*atan(tan(50)*4/5) = 87.3° horizontal, 2*atan(tan(50)*3/5) = 71.1° vertical. This is a hardware fact, not a fit: the fitted numbers this package shipped before are the alternatives beside it.

The screenshot is most likely a crop. Kept so the old coverage numbers can be reproduced.

top_camera_mount.hint: The mast that carries the top-down camera over the deck.

options.label: No overhead camera (stock LeKiwi)
options.note: Stock LeKiwi has no mast and no top camera - the deck is bare. The overhead view is this project's addition.

interface.note: the camera face of the PincOpen gripper, as that package publishes it

options.label: PincOpen camera holder (as assembled)
options.note: The camera stack upstream PincOpen ships: the basement bolted to the 4x M2 seat at Z 19.5, with the sliding support in it up to Z 104.9. It publishes NO camera pose, and that is a measurement, not an omission. The PincOpen package declares no sensor and no lens for this holder, and the camera face is a SEAT (four M2 at Z 19.50), not a sensor datum. The support slides, so there is no height to publish either. Fitting this therefore switches the wrist camera OFF: measure your own head and type the pose in under "As installed".

meshes.label: Camera retainer plate
meshes.note: The 58 × 26 retainer plate with its 24 × 14 cable window that clamps the DF200 into a camera head, print only. ONE plate serves every head this project builds: the corner mast and the DF200 wrist arch both draw their own retainer, and both name this one - the same solid to 0.005 mm, measured on the exported meshes. 2x M3 × 12 self-tapping into Ø2.60 × 9.50 pilots, 8.0 mm of bite.

meshes.label: Camera pocket shims
meshes.note: Depth shims behind the module, print only: 36 × 36 mm at 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.6 mm with the same 24 × 14 window. They stack to 2.8 mm in 0.4 mm steps, so a 9.5 or 10 mm camera still clamps solid in the 11.3 mm pocket. Shared by the corner mast and the wrist arch. Three shims on one plate, which is why the print check WARNs "3 bodies".

part.label: Corner mast, printed · 45°

meshes.label: Corner mast (printed) · lower spar + deck base
meshes.note: The deck plate and the tapered hollow spar in one part, Z 57 to the Z 285 spigot, with 3.5 mm walls. 4x M3 × 8 into M3 heat-set inserts in the deck grid, a Ø7.5 × 26 driver relief above every bolt, and two gusset fins fore and aft where the plate has room for them. 248.0 mm on the bed, so it needs 250 mm of Z: an MK4 (220 mm) will not take it, an Ender 3 (250 mm) has 2.0 mm to spare.

meshes.label: Corner mast (printed) · upper spar + yoke
meshes.note: Z 285 to the top of the index fan: the spar AND the yoke in one part. The tapered section grows the two hinge cheeks, the M3 × 60 hinge (54.2 mm of stack) and the 40..70° index fan directly - no collar, no seat disc, no clamp and no joint under the cheeks. 229.6 mm on the bed, 90.0 g, 337 mm² of bed contact.

meshes.label: Corner mast · camera head
meshes.note: The clamp block alone: 36.4 × 36.4 pocket, 3 mm lip, OPEN REAR, two ears. The tilt index seats are BLIND, 3.0 mm deep, and cut in BOTH side walls, which is what makes this ONE STL for the corner mast and the wrist arch. Prints lens face down on 975.8 mm² of bed contact, 5.5 % overhang. Support the two hinge-lug ends - a 23.7 mm bridge.

meshes.label: Corner mast · camera retainer
meshes.note: The 58 × 26 retainer plate with its 24 × 14 cable window, at its seated pose on the head's ears. NOT a plate of this set: print the shared "Camera retainer plate" upgrade instead. meshes.label: Corner mast · DF200 module (stand-in)
meshes.note: The JR DF200 module itself, as a volumetric stand-in: 36 × 36 × 11 body, Ø20 × 9 lens barrel, Ø13 × 3 hood, 9 × 5 × 4 rear connector, sensor 4 mm behind the front face. Seated in the pocket at the shipped detent, front face on the 3 mm lip, barrel through the 30 × 30 aperture. The connector is on the image-UP axis, so it passes the retainer's 24 × 14 window. Measured on the exported meshes: module n head 0.001 mm³, connector n retainer 0.000 mm³. The retainer boss presses the back face by 0.40 mm (206 mm³ - the clamp preload; a 0.5 mm pocket shim goes behind a thinner module). NOT a printable part: it is what you buy.

top.source: user-confirmed JR DF200 "100° without distortion", 640 × 480 MJPG 4:3, rectilinear -> 87.3° H / 71.1° V (2026-09-15)

part.notes: Sensor 538 mm above ground on the rear-left corner, 45° nose-down and panned 10°, so the arm crosses the view instead of running down it. At the DF200's real 87.3° the whole reachable floor and table are in frame at every detent, so the detent is picked to keep the ROBOT out of frame. 45° puts 4.6 % of the frame on the robot, against 8.6 % at 55°. Its near edge lands on the front wheels (Y 69 mm) and it still carries 3.2 m of context. No hardware store: a tapered PLA spar in two halves, pinned by 3x M3 × 8 at the Z 285 spigot, with no collar, no seat disc and no pinch clamp. 187 cm³ of spar. Tip deflection at 1 g is 0.298 mm fore-aft and 0.259 mm lateral, first mode 34.4 Hz. The taller half is 248.0 mm tall, so it needs 250 mm of Z.
